DETAIL: Reject. Preserve the prior repair requirement: encode protection coverage for each machinery installation and each associated equipment item, scoped to every applicable controlled hazard, with evidence substantiating that coverage. The six separate sh:hasValue/sh:minCount constraints incorrectly make all hazards conjunctively mandatory and do not model applicability; do not impose all six when only a subset is applicable. The candidate also has no coverage relationship or equivalent hazard-to-entity protection assertion, so hasApplicableHazard plus installation-level evidence is only a presence approximation. Its associated-equipment SPARQL checks merely that some installation links the item and has some evidence; it does not establish that the equipment itself is protected for each applicable hazard and is therefore the wrong semantic check. Preserve the authoritative owners: hasApplicableHazard, hasAssociatedEquipment, and hasHazardProtectionEvidence belong on machineryInstallationItem, while the required coverage assertion must relate the installation/equipment to the applicable hazard without relocating those properties to the ship or duplicating facts. A canonical coverage relationship or required cross-owner path is absent from the scoped vocabulary, so locate that canonical term/path and then encode the bounded static relationship and evidence constraints; do not use the ship-level hazardProtectionCoverage boolean.
